news.headline: Global Airspace Radar: Podcast with Karl Wannenmacher
EXCLUSIVE: Air traffic controllers will thrive with help from AI

paragraphs: Frequentis supplies communication and information systems for control centres with safety-critical tasks. The work splits between air traffic management, civil and military, and public safety and transport.

On the public safety side the buyers are police, fire brigades, ambulance services, coastguards and port authorities. Voice communication for air traffic control is the anchor, and the company puts its share of that market at around 30%. It also sells aeronautical information management and aeronautical message handling systems. Current development centres on digital remote tower technology, drone management and 5G/LTE in safety-critical applications.

The Austrian company is headquartered in Vienna and was founded in 1947. It keeps a network of branches, subsidiaries and local representatives in more than 50 countries. Around 550 customers in approximately 150 countries rely on its know-how, by its own count. Installed operator positions number around 49,000 worldwide. More than 75% of employees come from science, technology, engineering and mathematics backgrounds.

quote.text: Frequentis systems and solutions help make the world a safer place.
